messages.author: 8c869d2e28f4b8f9
messages.subject: Predictions using overdispersed Poisson regression
parts:
Hi fellow Stan-users

I'm using rstan 2.0.1 to calculate a Poisson regression with extra
variation and an offset. The model is quite like the "Salm"-example from
WinBUGS and I've taken some code from the Stan-code from that example.

The basic model runs great and produces sensible output.

But in a second step, I now want to make predictions using my model. In
WinBUGS/OpenBUGS/JAGS, this could be accomplished by simply setting some
observations to missing. This is not possible in Stan and I have
therefore followed the suggestions in the Manual and specified the
missings in the "parameter" block.

One problem I was facing is that the "poisson_log" function requires
integers which can't be set in the "parameter" block. So I tried to use
"increment_log_prob" to specficy the Poisson-likelihood directly.

Here is my code:

data {

    int<lower=0> N; // number of observed data points
    int<lower=0> suic[N];
    real jahr[N];
    int<lower=0> bev[N];

    int<lower=0> N_pred; // number of predicted data points
    int<lower=0> jahr_pred[N_pred];
    int<lower=0> bev_pred[N_pred];

}

transformed data {

  real jahr_mean;
  real jahr_centered[N];
  real log_bev[N];

  real jahr_centered_pred[N_pred];
  real log_bev_pred[N_pred];

  jahr_mean <- mean(jahr);


  for (i in 1:N) {

   jahr_centered[i] <- jahr[i] - jahr[1];
   log_bev[i] <- log(bev[i]);

  }


  for (i in 1:N_pred) {

    jahr_centered_pred[i] <- jahr_pred[i] - jahr[1];
    log_bev_pred[i] <- log(bev_pred[i]);

  }
}

parameters {

    real alpha_star;
    real beta;
    real<lower=0> tau;
    real lambda[N];

    real lambda_pred[N_pred];
    real<lower=0> suic_pred[N_pred]; // to be predicted; can't be specified as "int"

}

transformed parameters {

   real<lower=0> sigma;
   real alpha;

   alpha <- alpha_star - beta * jahr_mean;
   sigma <- 1.0 / sqrt(tau);

}

model {

   real lambda_obs[N];
   real lambda_miss[N_pred];

   alpha_star ~ normal(0.0, 1.0E3);
   beta ~ normal(0.0, 1.0E3);
   tau ~ gamma(0.001, 0.001);

   for (i in 1:N) {

    lambda[i] ~ normal(0.0, sigma);
    lambda_obs[i] <- alpha_star + beta * jahr_centered[i] + log_bev[i] +
lambda[i];
    suic[i] ~ poisson_log(lambda_obs[i]);

   }


  for (i in 1:N_pred) {

    lambda_pred[i] ~ normal(0.0, sigma);
    lambda_miss[i] <- alpha_star + beta * jahr_centered_pred[i] +
log_bev[i] + lambda_pred[i];
    increment_log_prob(suic_pred[i] * log(lambda_miss[i]) -
lgamma(suic_pred[i] + 1) - lambda_miss[i]);

   }
}


The model runs fine but  I'm not entirely sure if my implementation of
the predictions using Poisson models is sensible.

My specific question is:

  • Is my model sensible for predicting further observations? Or is there another method that would be recommended?

Thank you very much for you time and help.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Predictions using overdispersed Poisson regression
parts:
You can't use the Markov chain to generate samples because, as you note,
you need integer samples.  But, because the predictive samples are drawn
conditioned on the data, you can use the generated quantities block to 
create your samples assuming we have the right RNGs.  Luckily poisson_rng
is available in 2.0.1 so you should have no problems.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Predictions using overdispersed Poisson regression
parts:
I don't know what the effect is of treating the Poisson's
output as continuous.

You can just code up simple integer predictions like you're
trying to derive directly in the generated quantities block (after the
model) as:

generated quantities {
real<lower=0> suic_pred[N_pred];

+ lambda_pred[i]);

}

You don't need to increment the overall log prob (and in fact can't
from the generated quantities block), because it's not
going to affect the sampling.

It also looks like the variable you called "jahr_centered" is not
centering by subtracting the mean but is rather subtracting
the first element of jahr.

- Bob

messages.author: 8c869d2e28f4b8f9
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Predictions using overdispersed Poisson regression
parts:
Thank you very much, Bob and Michael for the quick reply.

That pretty much answers all my questions. First, I was unaware that "increment_log_prob" would increment the overall log prob. Second, I didn't know that one can use the random generators in the "generated quantities" block.

Regarding the "centering": That is indeed a relict from an earlier version were I did center the years. Thanks for noticing.

I get plausible output now using the following "generated quantities" block:

generated quantities {

     real suic_pred[N_pred];
     real lambda_miss[N_pred];
     real<lower=0> lambda_miss_exp[N_pred];

     for (i in 1:N_pred) {
       
      lambda_miss[i] <- alpha_star + beta * jahr_centered_pred[i] + log_bev_pred[i] + lambda_pred[i];
      lambda_miss_exp[i] <- exp(lambda_miss[i]);
      suic_pred[i] <- poisson_rng(lambda_miss_exp[i]);

    }
}

Thanks again for your help and have a nice day.

Serdash

On Sunday, November 24, 2013 12:50:46 AM UTC+1, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I don't know what the effect is of treating the Poisson's
output as continuous.

You can just code up simple integer predictions like you're
trying to derive directly in the generated quantities block (after the
model) as:

   generated quantities {
     real<lower=0> suic_pred[N_pred];
     for (i in 1:N_pred)
       suic_pred[i] <- poisson_rng(alpha_star
                                   + beta * jahr_centered_pred[i]
                                   + log_bev[i]
                                   + lambda_pred[i]);

   }

You don't need to increment the overall log prob (and in fact can't
from the generated quantities block), because it's not
going to affect the sampling.

It also looks like the variable you called "jahr_centered" is not
centering by subtracting the mean but is rather subtracting
the first element of jahr.

- Bob
